exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
Gestational age at birth (full-term vs. preterm)
Children with congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction (CNLDO)
outcome: Need for surgical intervention for CNLDO
cohort: 104 children diagnosed with congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction (CNLDO) at a tertiary referral center between 2012 and 2017
finding: Cesarean section (CS) is a risk factor for CNLDO, independent of gestational age, and children born via CS tend to have a more complicated clinical course requiring additional surgical interventions.
mod_finding: Cesarean section is a risk factor for congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction (CNLDO), independent of gestational age.
